gp.heading: Gross Profit (Loss)
gp.text: Gross profit was $3.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to a gross loss of $0.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. This marked the Company’s first quarter of gross profit, reflecting its first commercial product deliveries.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenue
cor.text: Cost of revenue increased to $1.6 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $1.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The increase reflects the scale-up of production operations at SN-0 as the Company qualified processes and manufactured its first commercial core. The $0.4 million increase comprised a number of individually smaller items, the largest of which was an increase in share-based compensation expense.

opex.text: Net Cash used in Operating Activities — Net cash used in operating activities increased by $8.2 million, from $2.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025 to $10.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting cash paid for costs of revenue and operating expenses as our business scaled, partially offset by cash collected from customers.

costs.text: Net Cash used in Operating Activities — Net cash used in operating activities increased by $8.2 million, from $2.8 million for the six months ended June 30, 2025 to $10.9 million for the six months ended June 30, 2026, primarily reflecting cash paid for costs of revenue and operating expenses as our business scaled, partially offset by cash collected from customers.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses
rd.text: Research and development expenses were $2.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to no research and development expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The expenses consists of internal labor and process engineering work to establish and qualify the manufacturing processes required to bring SN-TN and SN-ID into commercial production, including the preparation of the facilities' licensing and authorization deliverables required under the Company's OTA with the Department. This work supported the Department's approval of the Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis for both facilities and the commencement of Final Documented Safety Analysis preparation at each site, ahead of the Department's readiness review. This investment underpins the Company's replicable facility model, which is designed to bring a standard production facility online in approximately 11 months and to reduce the time and cost of each subsequent increment of capacity.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Costs
ga.text: General and administrative costs increased to $5.5 million for the three months ended June 30, 2026, compared to $1.0 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025. The $4.5 million increase was primarily attributable to a $1.6 million increase in share-based compensation expense, a $1.5 million increase in third-party consulting fees related to the Company’s transition to a public company, and a $1.4 million increase in payroll and related benefit costs. These increases reflect the build-out of the internal infrastructure required to operate as a public company, including the addition of finance, accounting, legal and compliance capability, incurred in advance of scalable commercial deployment .

gp.heading: Gross Profit (Loss)
gp.text: Gross profit was $1.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to a gross loss of $1.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This marked the Company’s second quarter of gross profit, reflecting its first commercial product deliveries.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenue
cor.text: Cost of revenue increased to $4.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $2.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The increase reflects the scale-up of production operations at SN-0 as the Company qualified processes and manufactured its first commercial reactor core. The $1.8 million increase was primarily attributable to a $1.2 million increase in engineering and related consulting fees and a $0.5 million increase in payroll and related benefit costs, offset by a $0.1 million decrease in production supplies and facility-related costs. The decrease in production supplies and facility-related costs includes a $0.5 million out-of-period adjustment that reduced depreciation expense for certain machinery and equipment at the Company's Idaho and Tennessee facilities that had not yet been placed in service. The remaining increase was comprised of a number of individually smaller items, the largest of which was an increase in software and technology costs.

opex.text: Net Cash used in Operating Activities — Net cash used in operating activities increased by $11.2 million, from $5.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $16.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting cash paid for costs of revenue and operating expenses as our business scaled, partially offset by cash collected from customers.

costs.text: Net Cash used in Operating Activities — Net cash used in operating activities increased by $11.2 million, from $5.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $16.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting cash paid for costs of revenue and operating expenses as our business scaled, partially offset by cash collected from customers.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses
rd.text: Research and development expenses were $1.4 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to no research and development expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2025 . The expenses consist of internal labor and process engineering work to establish and qualify the manufacturing processes required to bring SN-TN and SN-ID into commercial production, including the preparation of the facilities' licensing and authorization deliverables required under the Company's OTA with the Department. This work supported the Department's approval of the Preliminary Documented Safety Analysis for both facilities and the commencement of Final Documented Safety Analysis preparation at each site, ahead of the Department's readiness review. This investment underpins the Company's templated and replicable facility model, which is designed to bring a standard production facility online in approximately 11 months and to reduce the time and cost of each subsequent increment of capacity.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Costs
ga.text: General and administrative costs increased to $15.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $1.8 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The $13.7 million increase was primarily attributable to a $9.0 million increase in share-based compensation expense and a $3.5 million increase in payroll and related benefit costs. The remaining increase was comprised of a number of individually smaller items, the largest of which was an increase in business insurance expense. These increases reflect the build-out of the internal infrastructure required to operate as a public company, including the addition of finance, accounting, legal and compliance capability, incurred in advance of scalable commercial deployment .

nonint.text: Net Cash used in Operating Activities — Net cash used in operating activities increased by $11.2 million, from $5.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 to $16.6 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, primarily reflecting cash paid for costs of revenue and operating expenses as our business scaled, partially offset by cash collected from customers.

nonop.text: The Company recorded net other income of $2.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which is attributable to interest income, driven by the Company’s net proceeds from its July 2026 IPO. Net other expense was insignificant for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

The increase reflects a $13.7 million increase in general and administrative costs, $1.4 million of research and development expenses and a $1.8 million increase in cost of revenue, partially offset by a $5.1 million increase in revenue and a $2.0 million favorable change in other income, net.

Per share amounts are based on weighted average shares outstanding of 134,924,112 for the three months ended September 30, 2026, which mostly reflect the Company's post-IPO capital structure. In connection with the IPO, all outstanding shares of preferred stock converted into common stock, and the Company issued 10.0 million shares of Class A common stock in the offering. As a result, approximately 154.3 million shares of common stock were outstanding following the offering. Per share amounts for periods presented are therefore not comparable to periods following the offering.

intro.text: Standard Nuclear’s mission is to reliably deliver the essential building blocks of nuclear power at scale — enabling cost-effective, safe, and secure energy for the world. Standard Nuclear is focused on the large-scale production of advanced nuclear fuel and radioisotope power systems. It is the nation’s only independent manufacturer of TRISO fuel — a robust, high-performance fuel essential to advanced nuclear reactors for terrestrial, national security, and space applications. Standard Nuclear offers a reactor-agnostic supply of advanced fuels to the next-generation nuclear industry and delivers dependable radioisotope power solutions to the space and defense sectors. Through these efforts, it is helping to eliminate U.S. reliance on geopolitical adversaries for these strategically vital technologies. For more information, visit: https://www.standardnuclear.com.
